story: This image shows NGC 2477, also known as Caldwell 71, an open star cluster in the constellation Puppis. It holds about 300 stars and spreads across a patch of sky almost as large as the full Moon.

An open cluster is a group of stars that formed together from the same cloud and are only loosely held by gravity. Estimates put NGC 2477 at about 700 million years old. Because its members share a birthplace, they also share an age, which is how astronomers can speak of the age of the cluster as a whole.

Observers rate it highly, ranking it among the finest open clusters to be seen. It looks rather like a well-resolved globular cluster, but without the dense, crowded center that globular clusters have. Abbé Lacaille discovered it in 1751.
